properties.name: Los Alamos National Laboratory
properties.description: Nuclear weapon design laboratory responsible for providing research, development, and manufacturing guidance authority; plutonium pit production.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory
properties.description: Nuclear weapon design laboratory responsible for providing research, development, and manufacturing guidance authority.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Sandia National Laboratories
properties.description: Responsible for non-nuclear components of U.S. nuclear weapons; second campus at Livermore, California.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Kansas City National Security Campus
properties.description: Procurement and manufacturing of non-nuclear components for nuclear weapons.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Pantex Plant
properties.description: Nuclear weapon assembly, disassembly and high-explosive work; stockpile stewardship, nonproliferation, and safeguards and security missions.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Savannah River Site
properties.description: Manages tritium inventories and facilities; planned plutonium pit production; H-Canyon reprocessing (see fissile layer).

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Y-12 National Security Complex
properties.description: Production or refurbishment of complex nuclear weapon components and secondaries; national HEU processing and storage.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: Nevada National Security Site
properties.description: Former nuclear test site; subcritical experiments, nuclear and radiological emergency response training, support to national security customers.

prov.source: DoD Nuclear Matters Handbook 2020 (rev.) ch. 5

properties.name: AWE Aldermaston
properties.description: Site described by the regulator as covering the entire life cycle of nuclear warheads: research, design, component manufacture and assembly, in-service support, decommissioning.

prov.source: Office for Nuclear Regulation, defence sites: AWE Aldermaston

properties.name: AWE Burghfield
properties.description: Site where, in the regulator's words, warheads are assembled and maintained while in service and decommissioned when out of service.

prov.source: Office for Nuclear Regulation, defence sites: AWE Burghfield

properties.id: WP:sellafield windscale piles and calder hall
properties.name: Sellafield (Windscale piles and Calder Hall)
properties.description: Windscale piles produced military plutonium until the 1957 fire; the Calder Hall reactors produced military plutonium until 1989. Now a decommissioning and waste site.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: United Kingdom

properties.name: Chapelcross
properties.description: Reactors used to produce plutonium until 1964 and tritium thereafter; shut down 2003–2004.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: United Kingdom

properties.name: Capenhurst (gaseous diffusion plant)
properties.description: Gaseous diffusion plant that produced HEU for weapons from 1952 to 1962, then LEU for power reactors until 1982. The centrifuge plant on the same site is civil (Urenco).

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: United Kingdom

properties.id: WP:cea dam ile de france bruyeres le chatel
properties.name: CEA/DAM Île-de-France (Bruyères-le-Châtel)
properties.description: CEA centre that, in its own description, designs the nuclear charges of France's deterrent weapons and guarantees their safety and reliability; also hosts the DAM's high-performance computing.

prov.source: CEA, Les centres: DAM Île-de-France

properties.name: CEA Valduc
properties.description: CEA centre that processes and recycles the materials for the nuclear sub-assemblies of the deterrent's weapons, and operates the Epure radiographic facility under the France–UK defence treaty.

prov.source: CEA, Les centres: Valduc

properties.name: CEA Le Ripault
properties.description: CEA centre that designs and manufactures materials for the non-nuclear components of the deterrent's weapons, including pyrotechnic sub-assemblies and warhead casings.

prov.source: CEA, Les centres: Le Ripault

properties.name: CEA CESTA
properties.description: CEA centre responsible, in its own description, for the overall design of the warheads of the French deterrent; operates the Laser Mégajoule.

prov.source: CEA, Les centres: CESTA

properties.name: Marcoule (G1–G3, Célestin, Phénix)
properties.description: Graphite-moderated gas-cooled reactors G1–G3 produced plutonium until 1992; the two Célestin reactors (1967/1968–2009) and the Phénix fast reactor also produced weapon plutonium. Site continues as a civil research and waste-management centre.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: France

properties.name: Pierrelatte (military enrichment plant)
properties.description: HEU production ended in June 1996; the plant was shut down and is being dismantled. The Georges Besse II centrifuge plant on the Tricastin site is civil.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: France

properties.name: China Academy of Engineering Physics (CAEP)
properties.description: Research academy in Mianyang described by FAS as the primary design laboratory for Chinese nuclear weapons; on the U.S. Commerce Entity List since 1997 with its subordinate institutes.
properties.coord_source: Federation of American Scientists, China nuclear forces guide: CAEP
properties.coord_note: coordinate as given by FAS (31°28'N 104°46'E), tier 2

prov.source: Federation of American Scientists, China nuclear forces guide: CAEP

properties.name: Lop Nur nuclear test site
properties.description: China's nuclear test site; the Bulletin's Nuclear Notebook reports construction at the site and U.S. statements of concern about adherence to a zero-yield standard.
properties.coord_note: Lop Nur lake centroid, not the test base

prov.source: Kristensen, Korda et al., Chinese nuclear weapons, 2025, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (Nuclear Notebook)

properties.name: Jiuquan Atomic Energy Complex (Plant 404)
properties.description: Plutonium production reactor believed shut down in 1984; the complex continues with reprocessing capacity.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: China

properties.name: Guangyuan plutonium production complex (Plant 821)
properties.description: Reactor that, per IPFM, probably stopped plutonium production by 1989.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: China

properties.name: Lanzhou gaseous diffusion plant (Plant 504)
properties.description: Produced HEU for weapons; now operates as a civil enrichment facility producing LEU.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: China

properties.name: RFNC-VNIIEF (Sarov)
properties.description: Nuclear weapon laboratory listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007 among the enterprises of the nuclear weapons complex.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: RFNC-VNIITF (Snezhinsk)
properties.description: Nuclear weapon laboratory listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: VNIIA (Dukhov Institute), Moscow
properties.description: Institute for warhead design and non-nuclear components listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: Elektrokhimpribor (Lesnoy)
properties.description: Weapon assembly and disassembly plant listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: Instrument-Building Plant (Trekhgorny)
properties.description: Warhead assembly and disassembly plant listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: PO Start (Zarechny)
properties.description: Weapon disassembly facility listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: Novaya Zemlya test site
properties.description: Nuclear test site listed in Presidential Decree No. 556 of 27 April 2007.

prov.source: Podvig, Russian strategic nuclear forces blog: Presidential decree lists Russia's military nuclear facilities (Decree No. 556, 27 April 2007)

properties.name: Siberian Chemical Combine (Seversk)
properties.description: Plutonium production reactors at Seversk, all closed (IPFM lists every Russian production reactor as closed; the Seversk reprocessing plant closed in 2010). The isotope-separation plant continues to produce LEU.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: Russia

properties.name: Mining and Chemical Combine (Zheleznogorsk)
properties.description: Plutonium production reactor ADE-2 shut down in April 2010; a pilot demonstration reprocessing centre operates on the site.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: Russia

properties.name: Khushab production reactors
properties.description: Four production reactors at which, per IPFM, Pakistan's plutonium has been produced.
properties.coord_note: Khushab city centroid, not the complex

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: Pakistan

properties.name: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (CIRUS, Dhruva)
properties.description: CIRUS (40 MWt) produced weapon-grade plutonium and was shut down in 2010; Dhruva (100 MWt), commissioned 1985, continues to operate. A pilot-scale enrichment plant began operating in 1985.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: India

properties.name: Dimona reactor (Negev Nuclear Research Center)
properties.description: Israel does not confirm or deny a weapons program. IPFM describes a plutonium production reactor that is still operating and may now be run primarily for tritium production.

prov.source: IPFM, Countries: Israel

properties.name: Yongbyon 5 MWe reactor and experimental LWR
properties.description: The 5 MWe reactor resumed operation in 2021; a light-water reactor under construction since 2010 appeared to begin operating in late 2023, per the Nuclear Notebook.

prov.source: Kristensen, Korda et al., North Korean nuclear weapons, 2024, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (Nuclear Notebook)

properties.name: Punggye-ri nuclear test site
properties.description: Test site partially disabled in May 2018; the Nuclear Notebook reports reconstruction since 2022. No test has occurred since 2017.

prov.source: Kristensen, Korda et al., North Korean nuclear weapons, 2024, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (Nuclear Notebook)

properties.name: Hanford Site
properties.description: Produced plutonium for weapons from 1943 to 1987; only N Reactor operated after 1971. Its mission since has been cleanup under the 1989 Tri-Party Agreement.

prov.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Hanford Site history
